Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Boise ID
515 AM MST Wed Nov 25 2026

.UPDATE...Updated aviation discussion.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- Light valley rain and mountain snow in eastern Oregon into
  central Idaho tapering off by the mid afternoon. 

- Widespread precipitation and above normal temperatures on
  Thanksgiving Day through early Saturday. Gusty winds will occur
  across southern areas late Friday. 

- High snow levels above 7000 feet MSL by Friday will shift most
  precipitation over the region.

&&

.SHORT TERM /Through Friday Night/...
Issued 319 AM MST WED NOV 25 2026
A weak warm front will move through southeast Oregon this 
morning. Widespread cloud cover and elevated east/southeast 
winds are keeping temperatures warm this evening, with Baker 
City and Burns both above freezing as of 2am. A pocket of 
clearing in central Oregon could allow temperatures to drop 
below freezing before sunrise. Warm air and precipitation will 
move over these colder pockets, bringing a 10% chance of 
freezing rain to Burns this morning. Baker City and the I-84 
corridor will see rain as the predominant precipitation type. 
Snow levels will hover around 4500-5500 ft MSL through the 
morning, with hi-res models showing a few pockets of heavier 
precipitation at times through the morning. Valley rain showers 
and mountain snow showers will move into the Treasure Valley 
and the Central ID Mountains by mid-morning. Snow amounts will 
generally be light with less than an inch of accumulation today,
but localized higher amounts are possible in those heavier 
showers. Widespread warming and drying will occur by the early 
evening, with overnight clearing early allowing for fog 
formation in high terrain valleys.

A robust atmospheric river will then move onshore by Thanksgiving 
Day, with a band of heavy rain and high elevation mountain snow 
moving in from the northwest by the afternoon. Cold pools lingering 
in mountain valleys, primarily in northeast Oregon, will again 
present a threat for freezing rain. This could create difficult 
travel conditions on the I-84 corridor in Baker County and just 
northwest of Ontario, OR. Strong zonal flow aloft will allow for 
high winds aloft, so forecast reflects the potential shadowing and 
lower precipitation chances, especially in the Baker Valley and the 
Treasure Valley. This moisture plume will continue through the end 
of the short term, steadily increasing the precipitation chances
southward each day. The Magic Valley will finally see precipitation
by Friday evening. Warm air moving in from the south and west 
will elevate snow levels to 7500-8500 ft MSL by Friday, with 
most populated areas in the mountains seeing rain on Friday. 
Snow levels might be slightly lower around 6000-7000 ft MSL in 
northern Adams/Valley County. Total accumulations for higher 
elevation snow from Thursday to Saturday will range from 6-12 
inches above about 7000 feet in the Central ID Mountains and 
Wallowa Mountains. Gusty winds will also peak on Friday and 
Saturday on mountain summits and in high terrain southwest of 
the Snake River Valley with gusts up to 35-45 mph by Friday 
evening. Temperatures will be about 5-10 degrees above normal 
through the short term period.

&&

.LONG TERM /Saturday through Wednesday/...
Issued 319 AM MST WED NOV 25 2026
High pressure will build into the region on Sunday, bringing a 
brief respite from the wet holiday week. This looks to be short-
lived, as another shortwave trough moves into the region on Monday 
and Tuesday. This will bring slightly cooler temperatures, lower 
snow levels back down to 5000-6000 ft MSL, and another push of 
valley rain and mountain snow. Ridging will attempt to build back in 
on Wednesday, but a closed low just off the coast of California will 
move through the region, splitting the upper level flow and bringing 
cooler air and precipitation to the southern tier of the region. 
Model uncertainty remains on the timing and positioning of the low, 
but most solutions and ensemble members agree that the bulk of the 
precipitation will be to our south over the Desert Southwest. 
Current forecast keeps a 20-40% chance of precipitation over the 
region through Wednesday, with temperatures lingering slightly above 
normal. Interestingly enough, the potential for a hard freeze in the 
Boise metro area appears to still not occur by early December. This 
would be the latest freeze on record, with the previous latest 
freeze occurring November 16th, 2016.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z Wednesday through Thursday/...
Issued 512 AM MST WED NOV 25 2026

Generally VFR. Light rain and snow showers with low VFR/MVFR 
conditions will move into SE OR terminals early this morning, 
then over central ID mountains through the afternoon. Snow 
levels 4-5.5kft MSL. Mtns obscured in precip. Surface winds: 
E-SE 5-15 kt. Gusts to 25 kt possible, mostly in the Snake
Plain. Winds aloft at 10kft MSL: SW 20-40 kt. 

KBOI...VFR. A 10% chance of rain showers near the terminal this
morning. Surface winds: SE 7-14 kt, potential for afternoon 
gusts 20-25 kt this evening through overnight. 

&&
